title: Borrheus and Reformers: Scripture sometimes uses justification for sanctification
source_text: XXXIII. Et certe quum vox justificationis, etiam plerorumque Reformatorum judicio, in Scriptura eo sensu quandoque usurpetur, ut ipsam hominis sanctificationem videatur complecti, jure damnari non possunt, qui caeteroqui sanam doctrinam retinentes, hoc vocabulo notione in Verbo Dei consecrata utuntur, quod inter Reformatos fecit Martinus Borrheus, olim in Academia Basiliensi Professor, si vera sunt quae citari video ex illius Commentario in Gen. cap. 15. ubi haec verba illi tribuuntur, inter plura ejusdem generis: Ut igitur Beatus Paulus, in justificatione nostra, quum ait, Quos justificavit eos glorificavit, comprehendit omnia, quae ad reconciliandos nos Deo Patri, & ad renovationem nostri aptam assequendae gloriae pertinent, ut sunt fides, justitia Christi, & donum justitiae a Christo exhibitum, quo regeneremur ad implendam justificationem quam lex requirit, ita etiam nos omnia in hac causa, quae recuperatione justitiae & innocentiae continentur, complecti volumus. Haec autem quum traduntur, non nova, sed confessa omnibus & veteribus & nostris, sacrarum litterarum Professoribus, qui quidem recte & vere dicerent, traduntur: nisi fortassis quadam distinctione dicuntur a nobis, quam vulgo dicunt in hoc justificationis negotio, sed in re ipsa abesse dissensionem, nequaquam dubitamus. Etenim omnes in impiorum justificatione, haec comprehendi monent, Christum justitiam nostram; remissionem peccatorum morte illius nobis partam; Spiritum Sanctum ob imputatae & ascriptae justitiae Christi nobis donatum; quo freti & peccatorum gratiam nobis fieri per fidem credamus; & renovationem nostri, qua Deum syncere diligendo, mediitemur, &c. Sed liber iste nobis ad manum non est.
pass_a_gloss: And certainly since the word of justification, even in the judgment of most of the Reformers, is sometimes used in Scripture in that sense so that it seems to embrace man's sanctification itself, those cannot justly be condemned who, otherwise retaining sound doctrine, use this vocabulary in a notion consecrated in the Word of God, which among the Reformed Martin Borrhaus, formerly Professor in the Academy of Basel, did, if those things are true which I see cited from his Commentary on Gen. 15, where these words are attributed to him, among more of the same kind: As therefore blessed Paul, in our justification, when he says, Whom he justified, those he glorified, comprehends all things that pertain to reconciling us to God the Father and to our renovation fitted for obtaining glory—such as are faith, the righteousness of Christ, and the gift of righteousness exhibited by Christ, by which we are regenerated to fulfill the justification which the law requires—so also we wish to embrace all things in this cause that are contained in the recovery of righteousness and innocence. But when these things are handed down, not new things, but things confessed by all both ancient and our professors of the sacred letters who would speak rightly and truly, are handed down: unless perhaps they are said by us with a certain distinction which the vulgar say in this business of justification, but that dissension is absent in the thing itself we by no means doubt. For all warn that in the justification of the ungodly these are comprehended: Christ our righteousness; remission of sins procured for us by his death; the Holy Spirit given to us on account of the imputed and ascribed righteousness of Christ; by which relying we believe grace of sins is made ours by faith; and our renovation, by which sincerely loving God we meditate, etc. But that book is not at hand for us.
pass_b_english: Even many Reformers grant Scripture sometimes uses justification to cover sanctification.
Borrhaus (if citations hold): Pauline justify/glorify packs reconciliation, Christ's righteousness, regenerating gift—dissension verbal, not real.
